comments.text:
Most differences are minuscule. Some brands might have a few dozens of MHz clock speed more or less, or they offer better cooling solutions. Some have different power connector requirements and offer different output ports.

If you take the MSI RX 580 Gaming X+ 8G you can see that the clock speed is at a max of 1441MHz in overclock mode. The card offers 1 DVI port, 2 HDMI ports and 2 Display Ports. And it requires two 8-pin power connectors to run.

By comparison the Gigabyte RX 580 Gaming 8G has a clock speed of 1355MHz in OC mode. Has 1 DVI, 1 HDMI and 3 Display Ports. And requires only a single 8-pin power connector.

Aside from the output ports and connectors it's hard to tell what difference these cards will give you in performance, power draw and temperatures. You should look up some benchmarks and roundups for the cards that interest you. And also note that a lot of brands also have different versions of each card just to make it more confusing. MSI alone has 5 different RX 580's on offer.

DOOM should be played at 120fps if you're using a mouse.
The engine feels more sluggish than most at 60fps, even other Bethesda games feel fine, but DOOM 2016 needs to be run uncapped at higher framerates (90fps and up) to get the best experience.
Even if your monitor is only 60hz you get lower input lag at higher framerates. Do note though that I haven't tried this with Freesync, so that could make all the difference (especially if you have a Freesync range up to 75hz that would be a big improvement).
It's ironic that this is the case on the game that is definitely intended to be more of a twitch shooter than anything else on the market, but the good news is it's not that hard to achieve.

Where as Project Scorpio had to render an additional eight cars on the field, 24 in total. I can see a GTX 970 maintaining 4K/60FPS on high while obtaining smooth framerates.
